Anthropic released its latest AI model, Claude Opus 5.5. The new version comes about two months after the previous Opus model upgrade, in line with Anthropic's usual release cadence.

Anthropic Claude Opus 5.5

Anthropic currently offers several AI models under the Claude brand.

The three main models are Haiku (the smallest and cheapest), Sonnet (mid-sized and mid-priced), and Opus (the largest and most expensive of the three).

There are also Fable/Mythos, which offer even greater power at a higher price and represent the company's most advanced models.

This release upgrades the Opus model from version 5.0 to version 5.5.

Anthropic stated: "Opus 5.5 is the first model we've launched since we called for a slowdown in frontier development. As with previous models, it was tested by external evaluation bodies before release, including METR and Frontier Design. It scored the highest marks in our most comprehensive alignment testing to date."

Below is Anthropic's introduction to Opus 5.5's performance:

On coding, Anthropic's introduction reads as follows:

Opus 5.5 is particularly adept at handling large, complex tasks such as codebase migrations and audits. One early tester used it to review and fix a 200,000-line codebase in three hours, whereas Opus 5 took over 20 hours and used 2.5 times as many tokens. In an internal test, we asked Opus 5.5 and Fable 5.1 to translate HAProxy—software widely used to balance web server traffic—from C to Rust. Both rewritten versions passed nearly all of HAProxy's own regression tests, but Opus 5.5 completed the task in just 9.5 hours, compared with 12 hours for Fable 5.1, and at 51% lower cost. Opus 5.5 delivers frontier-level agentic coding performance at extremely low cost. At the default performance level on FrontierCode, it wins while costing only about one-fifth as much as GPT-6 Astra per task. On Terminal Bench 4.0, it matched Astra at roughly 40% of the cost; and on CursorBench, it beat GPT-5.6 Sol by 11 points at about one-third the cost.

In addition, Opus 5.5's pricing has been adjusted compared with Opus 5:

Opus 5.5 requires less compute than Opus 5, and its pricing reflects this. Our tests show that, at default settings, cost on typical workloads is 40% lower than Opus 5. Input and output tokens are priced at US$4 and US$20 per million respectively, 20% lower than Opus 5. Cache reads—which make up the bulk of cost for agentic and coding work—are priced at US$0.20 per million tokens, 60% lower than Opus 5. Opus 5.5's output speed is also over 30% faster than Opus 5. In addition to the price cuts, we have raised the five-hour usage limits on Pro, Max and Team plans. We are also offering usage-limit resets to subscribers, who can now save the reset and choose when to use it.

The new Claude Opus 5.5 model is now available. Looking ahead, Anthropic said the Claude Sonnet 5.5 and Claude Haiku 5.5 models would be "released in the coming weeks, also bringing a number of improvements in performance, efficiency and safety."
